stem: Sketch the graph of $xy={=a}$. It has two branches: draw one, lift your finger, then draw the other. Show how each branch behaves near the two axes.
solution: Write $xy=k$ as $y=\dfrac{k}{x}$. The number on the right of $xy=$ is $a$, and it is negative here.
Because $a<0$, $x$ and $y$ always have opposite signs, so one branch lies in quadrant II ($x<0$, $y>0$) and the other in quadrant IV ($x>0$, $y<0$).
Complete a short table, for example $x=\pm1,\pm2,\pm3$ (and any other value that divides $a$ exactly), and plot each pair. Check that $x$ and $y$ have opposite signs in every row.
$x=0$ gives no $y$-value (division by $0$) and $y=0$ is never produced (a fraction with a non-zero top is never $0$), so the graph has no point on either axis.
Join the points in each quadrant with a smooth curve. Each branch gets closer and closer to the axes but never touches or crosses them, so the axes ($x=0$ and $y=0$) are the asymptotes.
notes: Instrument fit: the book asks the student to join table points into two smooth curves and then describe the asymptotes; the freehand two-branch stroke is exactly that, and the widget rejects a stroke that runs through x = 0. asymptote-crossed is the only misconception this construction can show of the asymptote-is-met kind: joining the branches into one curve through the y-axis is the belief that the graph reaches its asymptote. Rows are negative so that wrong-quadrants means one thing here (the curve drawn in quadrants I and III, as when a negative divided by a negative or a negative times a positive loses its sign); it is mapped to sign-lost-testing-point because that is the only sign-handling error on this objective's list, though the likelier conceptual cause, sign-of-a-ignored, belongs to lesson objective 1-2 and is not on this list. continuous-means-has-breaks is a vocabulary reversal that a sketch cannot reveal, so it is not mapped. partial-coverage (one branch only), vertically-displaced and off-target are left unmapped: they have no single dominant cause. Grading is within about one grid square, so |a| of 3, 4 and 6 are used for clear separation; a = -6 puts the points at x = ±1 off the visible grid, which the stem tolerates (the curve is mostly inside). Anchor is ex6-4-6e (xy = -6, give the asymptotes); the first row is that exact function.
